entry_thesis: Nike reports Q4 FY2026 earnings June 30 AMC (5 days out). The core asymmetry is intact: consensus EPS of $0.11 sits materially BELOW Nike's own ~$0.19 guidance, so an in-line-with-guidance print beats consensus by ~70%. Since the premarket call ($41.82), the setup has IMPROVED on entry: stock is now $41.07 (-1.8% intraday) and traded to a fresh 52-week low of $40.805. NEW development since premarket: Nike appointed David Denton as CFO (announced 06-25) and reports surfaced of a China business reshuffle — the market reads the CFO change as neutral-to-slightly-negative ('won't speed up turnaround'), adding uncertainty. But the CFO news does NOT change the Q4 EPS-bar asymmetry, and bear capitulation is intensifying (BNP $23 target, down 48% from ATH). Options-implied move (~8.9%) remains only modestly above the 8.4% historical average, so the market is still NOT pricing a positive surprise. Base case ~62% Nike beats the $0.11 bar; market-implied ~48%.
risk: The new CFO appointment (David Denton, outside hire) introduces transition-period uncertainty and could signal deeper internal concerns about the 'Win Now' turnaround — management reshuffles before earnings can telegraph weakness. Nike misses the $0.11 EPS consensus (genuine demand collapse worse than feared) OR guides fiscal 2027 sales decline worse than the current 2-4% range, which would confirm the turnaround is failing and trigger a re-rating toward BNP's $23 target. China revenue deterioration beyond the expected ~20% decline, or destabilizing details from the reported China business reshuffle, would also break the thesis.
target_return: 12-18% in 1 week (post-earnings relief rally if consensus beat + stable fiscal 2027 commentary off fresh 52-week lows)
catalyst: Nike Q4 FY2026 earnings, June 30 2026 AMC. why_beats_spy: SPY is flat today (+31.96% since inception, ~$733) with no near-term directional catalyst. NKE offers a specific 5-day dated event (Jun 30 earnings) with a quantifiable probability edge: consensus EPS ($0.11) sits below the company's own guidance (~$0.19), creating an asymmetric bar where merely meeting guidance = a ~70% consensus beat. The pre-event setup has improved intraday (fresh lows, better entry), and options-implied move (~8.9%) is not pricing a positive surprise — so the asymmetry is intact. A relief rally off 52-week lows on a beatable bar has materially more upside than holding flat-SPY for the same week.
falsification_condition: Nike reports Q4 EPS at or below $0.11 AND/OR guides fiscal 2027 revenue decline worse than the current 2-4% range — this would prove the consensus was correctly cautious, the turnaround is failing, and the setup has no edge. A positive print (EPS > $0.11) with stable FY27 guidance would confirm the thesis.
